# Issue #23: environment overrides are ignored

`load_config(defaults, env)` should let any key in `env` prefixed with `APP_`
override the matching lowercase key in `defaults`, with values coerced to the
type of the default (int, float, bool, str). Currently overrides are ignored.

1| def load_config(defaults: dict, env: dict) -> dict:
   2|     """Return a copy of `defaults` where any env var APP_<KEY> overrides the
   3|     value for key <key> (lowercased), coerced to the type of the default."""
   4|     cfg = dict(defaults)
   5|     for name, value in env.items():
   6|         if not name.startswith("APP_"):
   7|             continue
   8| 
   9|         key = name[4:].lower()
  10|         if key not in cfg:
  11|             continue
  12| 
  13|         default = cfg[key]
  14|         if isinstance(default, bool):
  15|             text = str(value).strip().lower()
  16|             if text in {"true", "1", "yes", "on"}:
  17|                 cfg[key] = True
  18|             elif text in {"false", "0", "no", "off"}:
  19|                 cfg[key] = False
  20|             else:
  21|                 raise ValueError(f"invalid boolean value for {name}: {value!r}")
  22|         else:
  23|             cfg[key] = type(default)(value)
  24| 
  25|     return cfg

arguments.summary: Implemented environment overrides in `cfg/loader.py`: APP_-prefixed names are matched case-insensitively to existing default keys, values are coerced to the defaults’ types, and boolean strings are parsed explicitly with validation. Defaults remain copied and unknown/non-APP variables are ignored.
